Class ThermodynamicMigrationEngine

public class ThermodynamicMigrationEngine extends AbstractSimulationEngine

ThermodynamicMigrationEngine

Simulates human demographic migration driven by thermodynamic free power gradients using Onsager reciprocal transport equations across an H3 hexagonal spatial manifold.

Mathematical Formulation

For each spatial cell \(i\), its biophysical free energy potential \(\Phi_i\) is defined as: \[ \Phi_i = \frac{\text{Food}_i + \text{Water}_i}{\text{Pop}_i + 1} \] Between adjacent spatial cells \(i\) and \(j\), the potential gradient is: \[ \Delta \Phi_{ij} = \Phi_j - \Phi_i \] Mass flux follows the Onsager reciprocal relation: \[ J_{ij} = M_0 \cdot \Delta \Phi_{ij} \cdot \text{Pop}_i \] where \(M_0 \in [0.01, 0.20]\) represents mobility conductance.

Resolution Scalability (\(r \in [2, 7]\)) invalid input: '&' Algorithmic Optimizations

Algorithmic resolution scalability implementation for Resolution 7 (and rigorously valid for Resolutions 2 to 7):

  • Topological Adjacency \(O(1)\) (Ring-1): For all valid H3 grids (resolutions 2 to 7), neighbor search is flattened into a precomputed contiguous adjacency table (
    invalid reference 
    DeterministicSpatialAdjacencyTable
    ), eliminating all spherical trigonometry calculations and reducing comparisons from 42.4 billion to 1.88 million per tick (\(O(1)\) strict).
  • Dynamic Adaptive Spatial Binning Fallback: For synthetic or non-H3 test environments, the spatial bounding box size dynamically adapts to the search radius without combinatorial explosion.
